name: Chevrolet 350 LT-1 small-block V8 (RPO LT1), 1970 Corvette, 370 hp SAE gross
summary: A 5.7 L two-valve pushrod V8 with a cross-plane crank, 11.0:1 compression, a long-duration solid-lifter camshaft (317 degrees intake, 346 degrees exhaust advertised, 96 degrees overlap) and a 780 cfm Holley four-barrel on a high-rise aluminium dual-plane manifold. Rated 370 hp gross at 6000 rpm, it was the highest-rated small-block Chevrolet of the carburetted era and runs to a 6500 rpm redline; the cross-plane firing gives each bank's exhaust the uneven per-bank pulse spacing of an American V8.

variant.value: RPO LT1 in the 1970 Corvette: 370 hp at 6000 rpm and 380 lb-ft at 4000 rpm, SAE gross, 11.0:1 compression, four-speed manual only
variant.note: Chosen because 1970 is the 11.0:1 year with the full factory cam figures published (advertised durations, overlap and lifts, below), and the Corvette version because Chevrolet rated it 10 hp above the Camaro Z/28's identical engine. Wikipedia says 'there was no difference between the engines' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_LT-1); its small-block article attributes the Camaro's 360 hp to 'the Camaro's 'log' manifold exhaust system and points ignition', citing Gunnell, Standard Catalog of Corvette 1953-2005 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_small-block_engine_(first-_and_second-generation)). In 1971 the LT-1 dropped to 9.0:1 and 330 hp gross / 275 hp net (Wikipedia LT-1 article); that version is not modelled.

bore_mm.note: 'Bore and stroke: 4.00 x 3.48 inches' in the LT1 entry. Same in the corvettestory.com 1970 specification page ('Bore / Stroke: 4.00" / 3.48" (Standard, L46, LT1 350 Cubic Inch)', https://corvettestory.com/specs/1970-Corvette-specs-options.php) and Wikipedia's LT-1 infobox.

displacement_cc.note: 'Displacement: 350 cubic inches'. 4.00 x 4.00 x 3.48 x pi/4 x 8 = 349.8 cu in = 5733 cc (my calculation).

rod_length_mm.note: 'the 5.7 in (144.8 mm) rod used in all other small-block Chevrolet engines' (the 400 section, contrasting its 5.565 in rod). Not stated for the LT-1 specifically; the LT-1's forged rods are not said to differ in length.

compression_ratio.note: 'Compression ratio: 11.00:1'. corvettestory.com: '11.0:1 (L46, LT1 Engines)'. Wikipedia LT-1: 'The LT-1 had an 11.0:1 compression ratio'.

firing_order.note: 'Firing Order 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2' in the 1970 Corvette engine specifications. Wikipedia: 'All first- and second-generation Chevrolet small-block V8 engines share the same firing order of 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2'. Cylinder numbering: 'Most GM engines are left-bank forward and number their cylinders by alternating from bank to bank, going front to rear' (EngineLabs, https://www.enginelabs.com/engine-tech/engine/firing-order-swaps-whats-best-for-your-engine/), i.e. 1-3-5-7 on the left bank and 2-4-6-8 on the right. That general statement is applied to this engine (my application).

crank.value: Cross-plane (90-degree) four-throw crankshaft, forged steel, four-bolt main caps
crank.note: 'It featured a forged steel crankshaft, 4-bolt main caps'. The cross-plane layout is not stated on the page; it is the only layout that gives the sourced order with even 90-degree firing on a production small-block (inference).

firing_intervals_deg.note: Derived from the firing order on a cross-plane 90-degree V8 (my reasoning); confirmed with engsim pins on the definition.

valves_per_cylinder.note: 'OHV 2 valves x cyl.' Pushrods, stamped steel rockers, ratio 1.5:1 ('Rocker Arms Stamping, Steel Rocker Arm Ratio 1.5:1', corvettestory.com).

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 'Heads - Casting 3972186 ... 2.02 inch diameter intake valves 1.60 inch diameter exhaust valves 64cc combustion chamber'. Enthusiast restoration site about the 1970 Z/28, whose LT-1 is the same engine. Wikipedia's L46 entry gives the same '2.02 / 1.60 in' for the 1969-70 '186' heads.

camshaft.note: 'Orig 1970 LT1 Cam is part no. 3972178'. NCRS forum posts (seen only as search excerpts; NCRS refuses automated reading) say GM submitted these cam figures to the AMA in 1970 and that they appeared in Corvette News, February/March 1970; not opened, not relied on.

intake_duration_deg.note: 'Camshaft timing: Intake: 317 degrees, Exhaust: 346 degrees, Overlap 96 degrees.' Advertised (GM) duration; the lift it is measured at is not given. Same figures on my1970z28.com.

overlap_deg.note: With 317/346 and 96 overlap the lobe separation works out to 117.75 degrees at the advertised points (my calculation: ((317 + 346)/2 - 96)/2).

intake_lift_mm.note: GM figure 0.4586 in ('Lift: (Intake) 0.4586"' on Over-Drive; 'Intake - .4586" (includes lash - .024")' on my1970z28.com). I subtract the 0.024 in lash to get the valve's actual lift, 0.4346 in = 11.04 mm (my arithmetic and my reading of 'includes lash'). corvettestory.com gives a service lash of '.020 inch' inlet and '.025 inch' exhaust for the LT1, which disagrees with the 0.024/0.030 attached to the lift figures; the definition uses the 0.024/0.030.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: GM figure 0.4850 in 'includes lash - .030'; 0.455 in = 11.56 mm after lash (my arithmetic).

duration_at_050_deg.value: 242 intake / 254 exhaust at 0.050 in lifter rise, lobe separation 116 degrees
duration_at_050_deg.note: Forum post (user 69autoXr, April 2007): 'LT-1 should be 242/254 @.050", .458/.485" lift, and 116 lobe separation.' Not a GM document. A later post in the same thread gives the intake closing point as '85 ABDC' at '.006" valve lift assuming 1.5:1 rocker ratio'. Used for the definition's cam because the advertised figures alone do not fix where the lobes sit.

redline_rpm.note: 'Redline was 6,500 rpm but power fell off significantly past 6,200 rpm.' No ignition rev limiter is described; 6500 is used as the definition's limit.

idle_rpm.note: Not found in a source I could open. NCRS forum excerpts seen in search results mention a target of about 900 rpm; NCRS refuses automated reading, so they were not opened. The definition's 900 rpm is an estimate.

peak_power_kw.note: 'Horsepower: 370 @ 6000 RPM' = 275.9 kW (my conversion). Rating standard: SAE gross ('both of these being brake horsepower (bhp) gross hp ratings', Wikipedia LT-1). Gross ratings were taken on a bare engine on a test stand with 'free-flowing exhaust headers with no mufflers' and no accessories (https://ateupwithmotor.com/automotive-terms/47-gross-versus-net-horsepower.html). The NHRA factored the engine at 425 hp for class purposes (Wikipedia small-block article); not used.

peak_torque_nm.note: 'Torque: 380 @ 4000 RPM' (lb-ft, gross) = 515.2 N m (my conversion). corvettestory.com: 'RPO LT1 370 hp @ 6,000 RPM; Torque: 380 lb-ft @ 4,000 RPM'. For the Camaro Z/28 version Wikipedia gives 380 lb-ft at 4000 rpm and my1970z28.com '380 @ 4500 rpm'.

intake_type.value: Single four-barrel carburettor (Holley 780 cfm, list 3972121, vacuum secondaries) on a cast-aluminium high-rise dual-plane manifold
intake_type.note: 'Carburetor: Holley 780 CFM 4-barrel 3972121' and 'an aluminum intake manifold'. 'cast-aluminum, high-rise, dual plane intake' (my1970z28.com). 'a 780 cu ft/min vacuum secondary Holley four-barrel carburetor on a special high-rise aluminum intake' (Wikipedia small-block article).

throttle_dia_mm.note: '780-cfm 4 barrel carb with1.686 inch diameter primary and secondary throttle bores'. The single throttle of equal area is 85.6 mm (my calculation: 2 x 42.8 mm).

header_type.value: Cast-iron 'ram's horn' exhaust manifolds with 2.5 in outlets, one per bank, then dual exhaust
header_type.note: 'special 2.5" outlet ram's-horn exhaust manifolds in the Corvette, Delco transistor ignition and a low-restriction exhaust'. Over-Drive: 'a low-restriction exhaust system'. Pipe and muffler dimensions and whether the two sides are joined were not found.

exhaust_pipe_dia_mm.note: The 2.5 in manifold outlet; the pipe diameter downstream is assumed equal (my assumption).

years.value: LT-1 1970-1972 (Corvette and Camaro Z/28); this file describes 1970

missing: valve timing events (opening and closing angles) from a GM document; only advertised durations and overlap are factory, the 0.050 in durations and lobe separation are from a forum post
lift at which GM's advertised durations are measured
idle speed (NCRS forum refuses automated reading; the factory service manual was not found online)
intake runner length and diameter, plenum volume
exhaust manifold runner lengths, pipe lengths, muffler type
whether the dual exhaust has a balance pipe
rod length stated specifically for the LT-1

sources.what: Over-Drive Magazine 'Chevrolet Fact Center' 1970 Corvette fact sheet: per-engine specifications for the LT1 (bore and stroke, 11.00:1, 370 hp at 6000, 380 lb-ft at 4000, mechanical lifters, camshaft timing 317/346 degrees with 96 overlap, lifts 0.4586/0.4850, Holley 780 cfm 3972121, forged crank, 4-bolt mains). Enthusiast publication; the figures match the factory data quoted elsewhere.

corvettestory.com 1970 Corvette specifications: bore and stroke, 11.0:1 for L46 and LT1, rocker ratio 1.5, LT1 valve lash, forged crank, LT1 370 hp at 6000 and 380 lb-ft at 4000, firing order 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2. Enthusiast reference site.

Owner's restoration site for a 1970 Camaro Z/28 (the same LT-1 engine): cam part 3972178, 317/346 degrees, 96 overlap, lifts including lash (0.024/0.030 in), 1.5 rockers, head casting 3972186 with 2.02/1.60 in valves and 64 cc chambers, high-rise dual-plane intake, 780 cfm Holley with 1.686 in bores, Z/28 rating 360 hp at 6000 and 380 lb-ft at 4500.
Wikipedia, Chevrolet LT-1: bore and stroke, 11.0:1, Holley 780, solid lifters, 370 hp Corvette and 360 hp Camaro both gross with 'no difference between the engines', 1971 and 1972 ratings.

Wikipedia, Chevrolet small-block (first and second generation): common firing order, 5.7 in rod, LT-1 section (178 cam, high-rise aluminium intake, 2.5 in outlet ram's-horn manifolds in the Corvette, 6500 rpm redline), footnote on the Camaro's log manifolds (Gunnell, Standard Catalog of Corvette).
EngineLabs, 'Firing Order Swaps: What's Best For Your Engine?' (Mike Magda, 2017): the standard GM firing order and GM's left-bank-forward, alternating cylinder numbering.

CorvetteForum thread 'LT1 cam specs' (2007): 242/254 degrees at 0.050 in, 116 degree lobe separation, intake closing 85 ABDC at 0.006 in. Forum posts, not GM; used only for the lobe positions the factory figures do not give.
Ate Up With Motor, 'Understanding Gross Versus Net Horsepower Ratings': gross ratings were taken on a bare engine with free-flowing headers, no mufflers and no accessories.

vehicle.name: Chevrolet Corvette LT-1 sport coupe (1970, M21 four-speed)

curb_kg.note: 'Model 19437 Sport Coupe ... Total - Curb: 3,285; Shipping: 3,180 lb.', converted by me. This is the model's curb weight, not specific to the LT-1; the same page's power-to-weight table uses '370 Horsepower LT1 Engine: 3,577 lb.' for a four-speed car, a figure it does not define (perhaps a test weight).

gear_count.note: 'Turbo Hydra-Matic (Automatic) Transmission (Not Available with L46, LT1 Engines)'. '370 HP (RPO LT1) ... 4-Speed (2.20:1 low) ... 4-speed (2.52:1 low)' in the Corvette Action Center 1970 powertrain table (https://corvetteactioncenter.com/specs/c3/c3power.html).

gears.note: 'Close Ratio Four Speed M21 Transmission (Not available with Standard Engine) 1st Gear 2.20:1 2nd Gear 1.64:1 3rd Gear 1.27:1 4th Gear 1.00:1 Reverse Gear 2.26:1'. M20: '1st Gear 2.52:1 2nd Gear 1.88:1 3rd Gear 1.46:1 4th Gear 1.00:1'. Options table: M21 fitted to 4,383 cars (25.31%) across L46, LT1 and LS5; no LT-1-specific split found.

final_drive.note: 1970 Corvette Powertrain Combinations: '370 HP (RPO LT1) 350-Cu.-In. V8 Turbo-Fire 350 | 4-Speed (2.20:1 low) | 3.70 [std] | 3.55 [econ] | 4.11 [perf] | Air Conditioning Not Available | 4-speed (2.52:1 low) | 3.55 [std] | 3.36 | 3.70'. Corvette: Year by Year lists LT-1 axle choices '3.08:1, 3.36:1, 3.55:1, 3.70:1, 4.11:1, 4.56:1'.

wheel_radius_m.note: Coker Tire reproduction of the Goodyear Speedway Wide Tread F70-15 'designed to fit the classic Chevrolet Corvette. Specifically ... 1970, 1971 and 1972 Corvette': 'Circumference 82.5' (inches), with the caveat that dimensions are 'non-scientific and based on an inflated tire, mounted to a wheel'. Radius = circumference / 2 pi, my calculation.

tyre.note: 'Tire Size F70-15B-4PR Nylon - 2 ply'. Wheels '15 x 8.00'.

top_speed_kmh.note: No published top speed for the 1970 LT-1 found.
